The superplastic tension tests of as-received alloy specimens and hydrogenated ones with 0.1wt%H, 0.3wt%H and 0.5wt%H were first carried out on Zwick Z050 universal testing machine at 825℃ with an initial strain rate of 10 -3s-1. All the specimens were stretched to an elongation of about 100%.

The specimens were hydrogenated at 750 ℃ by holding in a pure hydrogen environment for 1h followed by air-cooling to room temperature. The hydrogen contents in the range of 0~0.5wt% were obtained by controlling the charging time.

The superplastic tension tests of as-received alloy specimens and hydrogenated ones with 0.1wt%H, 0.3wt%H and 0.5wt%H were first carried out on Zwick Z050 universal testing machine at 825℃ with an initial strain rate of 10 -3s-1. All the specimens were stretched to an elongation of about 100%.
After superplastic deformation, the stretched samples were dehydrogenated and all residual hydrogen contents of Ti-55 are less than 0.0125wt%
Therefore, the dehydrogenated specimens were subjected to tensile testing at 550 ℃ with an initial strain rate of 10 -2s-1.

TEM observations of as-received and 0.5H-dehydrogenated specimens after high- temperature tension are shown in Fig.4. The dislocation density in 0.5H-dehydrogenated sample is much higher than that in as-received one.

The dislocation density in 0.5H-dehydrogenated sample is much higher than that in as-received one. Meanwhile, the interaction and tangling of dislocations cause greater resistance to dislocation movement. According to the dislocation strengthening theory, more dislocation density plays an important role in strength increase.
According to the Hall-Petch relationship [19, 20], a smaller grain size can lead to a higher strength.
Actually, the grain boundary pinning effect hinders further dislocation movement [21]. The dislocation strengthening effect can be also improved.
The acicular α phases increase grain boundary area, which results in dislocation pile-up and deformation resistance increase. Therefore, a higher strength and less plasticity is obtained.
